patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents requesting prenatal care, reporting 2 months of increasing breast tenderness, nausea, a 6.6 lb weight gain, increased urinary frequency, and uncertainty about the date of her last menstrual period. She stopped taking oral contraceptives 6 months ago and has been trying to conceive with her husband since then. She believes she is pregnant and was happy to share this news with her husband last week.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Stopped oral contraceptives 6 months prior in an attempt to conceive.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Reports being in a stable relationship and actively trying to conceive with her husband.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with symptoms suggestive of early pregnancy.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I think I may be pregnant—I've had increasing breast tenderness for about two months, along with nausea, about a 6.6 lb weight gain, and increased urinary frequency. I'm also not sure about the date of my last menstrual period. I stopped my oral contraceptives six months ago and we've been trying to conceive.
Have you taken a home pregnancy test yet, and if so, what was the result?
“Not yet, I haven’t taken a home pregnancy test. I was hoping to confirm it through your evaluation since I’m not sure about my last menstrual period.”
Have you experienced any vaginal bleeding, spotting, or abdominal/pelvic pain?
“No, I haven’t had any vaginal bleeding or spotting, and I don’t have any abdominal or pelvic pain.”
Have you been vomiting, and if so, are you able to keep fluids down without feeling dizzy or lightheaded?
“No, I haven’t been vomiting. I do feel some nausea, but I’m able to keep fluids down and I haven’t felt dizzy or lightheaded.”
Have you experienced any burning or pain with urination, fever, or flank pain?
“No, I haven’t had burning or pain with urination, and I don’t have fever or flank pain. It’s mainly just the increased urinary frequency along with the breast tenderness and nausea.”
Have you been experiencing significant fatigue or tiredness?
“Yes, I have been feeling more tired than usual and my energy feels a bit lower, though I wouldn’t say it’s extreme fatigue.”
Have you ever had pelvic inflammatory disease, a prior ectopic pregnancy, or any pelvic/abdominal surgeries?
“No, I’ve never been diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease, and I’ve never had an ectopic pregnancy. I also haven’t had any pelvic or abdominal surgeries.”
[DDX] Early intrauterine pregnancy, Ectopic pregnancy, Post-oral contraceptive amenorrhea/hormonal imbalance, Hypothyroidism, Pseudocyesis
